stories.title: Bitcoin Lightning patches one flaw, but a critical Linux bug stays open
stories.summary: Developers released a security update for the Bitcoin Lightning Network that closes one vulnerability, CryptoSlate reports. A separate, critical flaw in Linux remains unpatched. The source does not say how the Linux flaw could affect Lightning nodes.
stories.whyItMatters: Lightning Network security affects the safety of funds on Bitcoin's main payment layer, so any open flaw deserves attention.
whatToWatch: A patch or advisory for the Linux flaw
Guidance from Lightning node software on mitigating the exposure
questions: Which Linux component carries the flaw?
Do node operators need to act now?

stories.title: Nigeria tells dollar-stablecoin issuers to localize or lose retail access
stories.summary: Nigerian authorities have signaled that dollar-pegged stablecoin issuers must localize operations or risk losing access to retail customers, CryptoSlate reports. This is part of Nigeria's broader stance on foreign-currency stablecoins. The source does not give a compliance deadline or detailed rules.
stories.whyItMatters: Nigeria is one of Africa's largest crypto markets, so this stance could reshape how dollar stablecoins reach retail users there.
whatToWatch: Formal rules or a deadline from Nigerian regulators
Issuer responses, including local partnerships
questions: What does 'go local' require in practice?
Which issuers face the most exposure?

sources.title: Nigeria tells dollar-stablecoin issuers: go local or lose retail access

stories.title: Two Bitcoin miners report nearly $2 billion in profit, led by non-cash gains
stories.summary: Two Bitcoin mining companies reported close to $2 billion in combined profit, CryptoSlate reports. The largest driver was not cash, pointing instead to a non-cash gain, such as a rise in the value of Bitcoin held on their books. The source does not name the miners or break out the figures.
stories.whyItMatters: Profit driven by unrealized Bitcoin gains, rather than cash from operations, shows how tightly miner results now track Bitcoin's price.
whatToWatch: Individual earnings filings that break out cash versus non-cash profit
Whether either miner sells holdings to lock in gains
questions: Which two miners does this refer to?
How much of the profit is unrealized?

stories.title: US drops a proposed crypto rule, while EU oversight can still delay small transfers
stories.summary: US regulators have dropped a proposed crypto rule, CryptoSlate reports. The report contrasts this with Europe, where oversight can still hold up a transfer as small as $500. The source gives no further detail on the dropped US rule or the EU mechanism.
stories.whyItMatters: The contrast shows a widening gap between US and EU oversight of crypto transfers, which affects how easily funds move across borders.
whatToWatch: Any replacement rule from US regulators
EU guidance clarifying transfer-hold thresholds
questions: Which US rule was dropped, and by which agency?
What EU rule allows a hold on a $500 transfer?

stories.title: Coinbase's Base blockchain gets faster, but some apps still get no data
stories.summary: Coinbase's Base blockchain has become faster, CryptoSlate reports. Some applications can still connect to the network but receive no data, pointing to a lingering compatibility or infrastructure issue. The source does not name the affected apps or the cause.
stories.whyItMatters: Reliability problems on Base could affect developers and users who depend on the network for trading or payments.
whatToWatch: A fix or statement from the Base team on the data issue
Reports from affected app developers
questions: Which applications are affected?
Is the data gap tied to the speed upgrade?

stories.title: Bitcoin traders face an eight-hour data gap as Deribit prepares to delay market data
stories.summary: Deribit, a major crypto options exchange, is preparing to delay the release of key market data, creating an eight-hour blind spot for Bitcoin traders, CryptoSlate reports. The source does not say why Deribit is making this change or when it takes effect.
stories.whyItMatters: Deribit is a primary venue for Bitcoin options pricing, so a data delay could reduce transparency for traders managing risk.
whatToWatch: Deribit's official announcement with an effective date
Trader and market-maker reaction to the delay
questions: Why is Deribit delaying this data?
Which specific data sets are affected?

stories.title: Jito launches a paid Solana data feed offering early sight of trades
stories.summary: Jito has introduced a Solana data feed that charges for earlier access to trade information, CryptoSlate reports. The move puts a price on seeing transaction activity before it is broadly available. The source does not detail pricing or the intended customers.
stories.whyItMatters: Paid early access to trade data raises fairness questions on Solana, since it could give paying users an edge over other participants.
whatToWatch: Pricing and access details from Jito
Trader and developer reaction over fairness concerns
questions: Who can buy access to this feed?

stories.title: Coinbase now accepts tokenized gold as loan collateral, but its price feed pauses on weekends
stories.summary: Coinbase now lets tokenized gold back a loan on its platform, CryptoSlate reports. The price feed used to value that collateral does not update on weekends. The source does not say how this gap is handled for loan risk during weekend price moves.
stories.whyItMatters: Tokenized gold expands what can back crypto loans, but a weekend pricing gap could leave borrowers and lenders exposed if gold's price moves while the feed is frozen.
whatToWatch: Whether Coinbase addresses the weekend pricing gap
Loan terms covering weekend price risk
questions: What happens to a loan if gold's price moves sharply over a weekend?
Which oracle supplies the price feed?

stories.title: Crypto crime-tracking firm restores main tools after breach exposed user login data
stories.summary: A major crypto crime-tracking company has restored its main tools after a hack exposed login data for all its users, CryptoSlate reports. The source does not name the firm or explain how the breach occurred. The exposure of login data suggests affected users may need to reset credentials.
stories.whyItMatters: This firm's tools are widely used by investigators and compliance teams, so a breach of its systems raises questions about the security of crypto crime investigations.
whatToWatch: Full disclosure on the breach's cause and scope
Guidance for affected users on resetting credentials
questions: Which firm was breached?
Was any data beyond login credentials exposed?

sources.title: Crypto’s crime-tracking giant restores its main tools after hackers exposed every user’s login data
